# Tic Tac Toe — Design Document

**Date:** 2026-10-12
**Author:** Spec generated by human partner (builder)
**Status:** Draft → pending builder check

## Intent and the Why

A minimal, delightful two-player Tic Tac Toe that two people can play
face-to-face on a shared screen or pass-and-play on a single keyboard.
The experience should get out of the way: launch it, tap a square, and
play. No accounts, no network, no setup.

## Goals

- ✅ Local-only, zero network requests beyond initial shell.
- ✅ Two players, X (first) and O (second), alternating turns.
- ✅ Clear win/draw detection with a visible result line.
- ✅ Keep score across rounds; resettable.
- ✅ Runs in any modern browser (desktop + mobile).
- ✅ Fast feedback: each tap registers instantly, no perceptible lag.

## Non-Goals

- ❌ Online/multiplayer over the network.
- ❌ Single-player vs an AI/CPU opponent.
- ❌ User accounts, progress persistence, or cloud sync.
- ❌ Leaderboards, social sharing, or analytics.

## Anti-Goals (things that would make this a failure)

- **Perceived lag** — the board must feel snappy. A click should mark a
  square within one frame.
- **Unclear state** — it must always be obvious whose turn it is and
  whether the game is over.
- **Over-engineered** — no configuration screens, themes, or settings.
  Defaults should be good enough.

## Constraints

- Stack: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite. No other frameworks.
- Build target: ESM, bundled to `dist/`, served by a plain static server
  (or opened directly via `file://` / Vite dev server).
- Single HTML page; the whole app is one route.
- No external API calls. No runtime secrets.

## Decisions (builder calls, documented for review)

The human partner left these to the builder. Each is marked as such.

1. **State container** — React `useState` + `useReducer` for turn/game
   state. No Zustand/Redux; the scope doesn't justify them.
   *Rationale: minimal bundle size, simplest mental model.*

2. **Winning logic** — explicit array of 8 winning index triples over a
   flat 9-element board array. Simple, testable, and impossible to get
   wrong.

3. **Styling** — plain CSS modules (co-located `.module.css`). No Tailwind,
   no component library. Keeps deps thin and the look intentionally
   spare.

4. **Responsiveness** — CSS grid + relative units; board fills the
   smaller viewport dimension. Touch targets ≥ 48px.

5. **Score persistence** — none. Score resets on page refresh. A reset
   button clears it mid-session. *Rationale: persistence isn't a goal;
   sessionStorage would add complexity for little value.*

6. **Sounds/animations** — a subtle fade/scale on a winning line and a
   brief mark-place animation. No sound library (the browser's native
   short beep via `AudioContext` is acceptable but optional and gated
   behind a flag the user can ignore).

## Data Model

```
type Player = 'X' | 'O';
type Cell = Player | null;
type Board = [Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell];
// indices: 0|1|2 top row, 3|4|5 mid, 6|7|8 bottom

type GameState = {
  board: Board;
  currentPlayer: Player;
  winner: Player | null;
  winningLine: number[] | null; // indices forming the winning triple
  moves: number;               // count of marks placed
  draw: boolean;               // true when board full, no winner (builder call)
};
```

## Game Flow

1. App loads with an empty board, `currentPlayer = 'X'`, `winner = null`.
2. Player taps an empty cell → cell fills with their mark, `moves++`,
   `currentPlayer` toggles.
3. After every move, check for a win (8 triples) or a draw (`moves === 9`
   with no winner).
4. On win: set `winner` and `winningLine`; highlight that line; stop play.
   On draw: set `winner = null` but mark the board `draw = true`; show
   "Draw".
5. A "Restart" button clears the board to step 1 (keeps the running
   score) — available at any state (even mid-game) so players can start
   fresh without hunting. A "Reset Score" button clears score too —
   shown only when a game has concluded (draw or win).

## UI Layout (single view)

```
+---------------------------+
|  Tic Tac Toe              | <- title + status line
|  Score: X 2  -  O 1        |
|                           |
|   +---+---+---+           |
|   | 0 | 1 | 2 |           |
|   +---+---+---+           |
|   | 3 | 4 | 5 |           |
|   +---+---+---+           |
|   | 6 | 7 | 8 |           |
|   +---+---+---+           |
|                           |
|  [ Restart ]  [ Reset    | <- only when game over
|    Score ]                |
+---------------------------+
```

- Status line: "X's turn" / "O won!" / "It's a draw".
- Winning line cells get a distinct highlight color.
- Buttons are disabled/hidden appropriately (Reset Score only appears
  when a game has concluded).

## Tests

- `game.test.ts`: pure functions — `checkWinner`, `togglePlayer`,
  `isDraw`.
- `Board.test.tsx`: render + click → mark appears, turn toggles.
- No E2E needed at this scope; if added, cypress is the natural choice
  but it's a non-goal for v1.

## File Structure

```
dist/                      # build output (generated)
public/
  favicon.svg
src/
  components/
    Board.tsx
    Cell.tsx
    Status.tsx
    Controls.tsx
  hooks/
    useGameState.ts        # game logic as a custom hook
  lib/
    game.ts                # pure functions: checkWinner, etc.
  App.tsx
  main.tsx
  index.css                # global reset + tokens
  App.css / App.module.css  # layout
  game.test.ts
  Board.test.tsx
package.json
tsconfig.json
vite.config.ts
```

## Build / Run / Deliverables

**Build tool:** Vite (already chosen above).

**Commands:**
- `npm install` — install deps (react, react-dom, vite, vitest, @testing-library/react).
- `npm run dev` — start dev server at `http://localhost:5173`.
- `npm run build` — production bundle into `dist/`.
- `npm test` — run unit/component tests once.
- `npm run test:watch` — watch mode.

**Dependencies (minimal):**
- react, react-dom
- vite (dev)
- vitest, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom
  (dev, for tests)

**No linting/formatting enforced** beyond Vite's internal esbuild
transparency — keeping the tooling surface small. (Prettier/ESLint would
be a reasonable future enhancement but aren't a goal here.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm install && npm run dev` opens a playable board in a fresh
  browser.
- [ ] X and O alternate; a cell can't be taken twice.
- [ ] A win lights up a line and halts the game; status reads "<P> won".
- [ ] Filling the board with no winner shows "Draw".
- [ ] Restart clears the board but keeps the score; Reset Score zeroes
  the score.
- [ ] Layout works on a phone (landscape) and desktop.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Open Items / Explicit Delegations to Builder

- Exact color palette (X/O marks, board lines, highlight). Default:
  neutral grays with a blue accent — easy on the eyes.
- Font: system sans-serif (`system-ui`) — no webfont downloads.
- Win-line animation style. Default: a soft pulse + scale on the line.
- Sound: intentionally omitted; the builder may add a one-line optional
  beep if time permits, otherwise skip.
- **Restart button** is available at any time (not only at game over);
  **Reset Score** is gated to game-over states only.
